author: Declaration Desk
title: India in final talks to sell Philippines five more BrahMos missile systems, report says
dek: The deal could be worth up to $800 million, about twice the first order. Manila, locked in a dispute with China in the South China Sea, has confirmed it wants more.
body:
India is in the final stage of talks to sell the Philippines about five more BrahMos supersonic cruise missile systems, a deal worth $700 million to $800 million, a report said on Thursday, citing three sources with direct knowledge of the negotiations.

The order, of nearly 60 missiles in all, would be about twice the value of the $375 million contract the two countries signed in 2022, which made the Philippines the first foreign buyer of the missile. The report said two Indian sources gave the value. India's defence and foreign ministries and the maker, BrahMos Aerospace, did not respond to requests for comment.

## What Manila has said

The Philippine government has confirmed its interest on the record. Arsenio Andolong, the Philippine defence ministry's spokesperson, told reporters that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr had "expressed his desire to acquire additional BrahMos missiles", without giving details.

On Wednesday, Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, speaking by video to the Delhi Defence Dialogue in New Delhi, said Manila hoped to secure more BrahMos units and had shared a wish list with Indian officials to tailor the system to Philippine conditions, the report said. One Indian source told reporters that Manila now viewed India "as a very reliable partner".

The report said India is close to completing deliveries under the 2022 contract, which was for naval use. The first batch arrived in April 2024.

## The China factor

The Philippines is strengthening its coastal defences as its dispute with China over the South China Sea escalates, with repeated confrontations between the two countries' vessels around contested shoals in recent years. BrahMos is one of the world's fastest cruise missiles and can be fired from land, sea and air.

China has not commented on the latest report. When the first batch was delivered in April 2024, Wu Qian, a spokesman for China's defence ministry, said "defence and security cooperation between countries should not harm the interest of any third party", according to a report at the time. Beijing told the Philippines this week to rein in politicians it accused of crossing China's "red lines".

## Why it matters for India

A larger Philippine order would be a sign that India's push to become an arms seller is gaining ground. India's defence exports reached Rs 38,424 crore ($4.11 billion) in the year to March, up more than 62% from the year before, the report said, citing government data. New Delhi announced BrahMos supplies to Indonesia in July and has signed a deal with Vietnam; talks are reported with the UAE, Thailand, South Africa and Brazil. Demand rose after India used the missile in combat for the first time during last year's four-day conflict with Pakistan, the report said.

The sales also carry strategic weight. By arming South-East Asian states that have maritime disputes with China, India deepens its ties with ASEAN countries under its Act East policy, but it also risks being seen in Beijing as taking sides in the South China Sea at a time when New Delhi and Beijing are trying to steady their own relations along the Line of Actual Control. BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, which India still relies on for much of its military equipment.

## What happens next

No contract has been signed, and the figures could change before one is. The report did not give a timeline for signing or delivery, or say which Philippine service would operate the new systems.
